findings.title: Client-specific permission check does not fall back to all-clients permission when a resource already exists
findings.body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the all-clients type resource is consulted only when no resource named after the client's ID exists. If a client-specific resource exists (for example because another scope was granted or a resource was left behind), the method evaluates only that resource. A valid permission on the Clients type resource is then ignored for the requested scope, so an administrator who has an all-clients permission can be denied for that client.

findings.title: Null type resource causes NullPointerException in client permission check
findings.body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) can return null when the realm does not support the admin authorization schema or when the Clients type resource has not been created. The following call authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) does not check for null, so the permission check throws NullPointerException instead of returning false.

findings.title: Provider event listener can invoke unsupported V2 setPermissionsEnabled
findings.body: registerListener executes cleanup only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. However management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If both features are enabled, removal events call V2 implementations such as ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throw UnsupportedOperationException. This can break provider event processing or leave old permission data uncleared. The listener should be skipped when V2 is active or should explicitly use the V1 management implementation.

findings.title: getScope can NPE for missing or unknown resource type
findings.body: In AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope, when the authorization schema is supported, the code dereferences SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without verifying that the map lookup returned a ResourceType. A null or unknown resource type causes a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) rather than a ModelValidationException.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with Clients scopes/resources
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is not null. Realms that were initialized before this change therefore do not get the new client scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) or the Clients all-resource. Existing deployments can then fail scope lookups or evaluate client permissions incorrectly after upgrade.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission can return the resource-type name and misses all-clients grants
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every resource of type Clients that grants the scope. This includes the type resource named 'Clients', so the returned set can contain the literal string 'Clients' instead of a client ID. It also only includes individually created client resources; if the caller has an all-clients permission but no individual client resources exist, no real client IDs are returned, which can make client filtering/listing incorrect.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve client resources
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName only special-cases Users. For Clients resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but client resources are created with the client's UUID as the resource name and no display name. As a result, client permissions/resources may be represented with null or raw UUID names instead of a readable client identifier or 'All clients'.

findings.title: Missing coverage for all-clients permission when a client-specific resource exists
findings.body: The new tests exercise single-client permissions and all-client permissions separately, but do not test the case where a client-specific authorization resource already exists and an all-clients permission should still grant access. That scenario covers the fallback logic in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission and would catch regressions where all-clients permissions are ignored once a specific resource exists.
